title: This Bizarre Jurassic “Squid” Swam the Ancient Seas of Wyoming - Nautilus
author: Devin Reese
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementZoologyThis Bizarre Jurassic “Squid” Swam the Ancient Seas of WyomingAnd likely gobbled up its smaller cephalopod relatives for lunchDRBy Devin Reese1:00 PM CDT on October 30, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleJason PooleIn Wyoming, we find cowboys, bison, rodeos, elk, and natural hot springs. But ocean cephalopods?A recent study published in Papers in Palaeontology reported a new species of cephalopod: Wyoteuthis linsterorum (Wyoteuthis = “a squid from Wyoming”). It’s a belemnite, a now-extinct group of squid and octopus relatives. Its fossils were unearthed at the Sundance formation, a set of rocks dating to about 160 million years ago, and then stored in museum collections until paleontologists recognized their uniqueness.Belemnites had been found in this fossil formation before, since it used to be an inland sea during the Jurassic, connected to the Pacific Ocean. But never had a belemnite this big turned up. In fact, it was the chunkiest belemnite ever found, based on the 2.4-inch girth of its rostrum, a bullet-shaped shell that protected its soft body parts.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
